name: Lacustrine-Fastness
description: Glacier upon glacier, blue-white and creaking, buried in places by nitrogen snow. The shell is broken in places by an ancient meteor crater, and through those breaches the deep ocean breathes plumes of frost into the dark.

There is a hush that is not emptiness but attention, as if the landscape were listening back. Visitors report dreams of falling that persist for days after departure. Mats of pigment-bearing microbes stain the wet stone in bands of rust and violet.
Instruments disagree about the signal of unknown origin: mass reads one value, inertia another. Probes sent in return transmitting their own launch signals, timestamped hours early.
Research vessels hold position at a respectful distance and take turns being unnerved. The anomaly, for its part, seems patient.
